Mutation report for run 20261116-123523.

Limits of this report.
A test that caught nothing has shown no way to fail against these bugs. That is a question to look at, not proof the test is empty.
A check that sits after an earlier failing REQUIRE in the same test may never have run.
Each verdict comes from one run of its bug, so it reads "caught in its run" or "survived its run". A bug in threaded code, or one that reads past the end of memory, may land either way in another run.
No tool can say whether a survivor is an equivalent bug, one that changes nothing a user could see.
A bug the tests found by crashing the test program counts as found; the test that was running is named on the bug's line, and is credited as a catch only if run.py's sort_red_tests sorted it so.
A test that went red in the mapping run, with every switch off, is red with no bug and is left out of every bug.
